\chapter{Synthesis --- Telling What Happened}
\label{ch:sintesis-preterito-completo}
\hlchaptermodality{205}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can tell a short past story about other people.}

I can tell a short past story about other people.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Synthesis — telling what happened}

\label{lesson:ES-C55-sintesis-preterito-completo}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Hablaron}. \emph{Fueron}. Two plurals, two different bargains — one regular, one refusing every ending in the language.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Three chapters ago your past tense could still only talk about \textbf{one person at a time}. Now it can talk about a group:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{Hablaron español.} & They spoke Spanish. \\
\emph{Comimos en casa.} & We ate at home. \\
\emph{Tuvieron tiempo.} & They had time. \\
\emph{Fueron profesores.} & They were teachers. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

That is the difference between keeping a diary and \textbf{telling a story}. A story needs other people in it, and other people need a plural.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the form that pays twice}]
One of the five forms you just learned is about to do a second job.

\begin{quote}
\emph{hablaron} · \emph{comieron} · \emph{tuvieron} · \emph{fueron}
\end{quote}

\textbf{Swap the \emph{-ron} for \emph{-ra}} and something appears that Spanish uses for supposing: \emph{hablara}, \emph{comiera}, \emph{tuviera}, \emph{fuera}. That is the form the next chapters need — the one that lets you say \emph{if I had time} rather than \emph{if I have time}.

You are not learning it yet. You are being told that \textbf{you already own the raw material}, which is why the plural had to come first.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Hablaron español y tuvieron tiempo}
  \item \emph{Fueron profesores}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What can this tense do now that it could not before? (Talk about \textbf{other people} — tell a story rather than keep a diary.)

And which form is about to be used twice? (The \emph{\textbf{they}} form.)
\end{tcolorbox}
